newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currencies end lower on U.S. comments.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currencies end lower on U.S. comments.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mostly lower after comments from U.S. Treasury department officials helped push marks and yen lower, traders said.

U.S. deputy Treasury secretary Lawrence Summers, whose comments on Wednesday supported the rally in currencies, said a strong currency was very much in U.S. interests. Summers' statements followed U.S. Treasury secretary Robert Rubin's comment that U.S. dollar policy was unchanged.
In addition, several European officials soothed EMU jitters and weakened marks safe-haven status ahead of the June 16 Amsterdam summit.
"The dollar rises when we get less worried about the EMU (European monetary union)," one currency futures floor analyst said.

September marks fell to $0.5819, near support at $0.5816 or 1.7312 spot marks. Critical support rests at $0.5810 or 1.7327 spot. Earlier the contract cut losses, but failed to rise near the pivot point of $0.5873.
The downside momentum in most currency pits started on Wednesday's overnight GLOBEX session when September yen lost nearly $0.000400 to $0.008730, below the 200-day moving average.

However, the new French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said he and European Commission president Jacques Santer made progress on an EU budget discipline pact. France said its concern to redirect European economic policy towards promoting growth and jobes had been understood.
The jobs issue will be the focus of a key Franco-German summit in western France on Friday, French president Jacques Chirac's spokeswoman said.
Jospin will also talk to British prime minister Tony Blair later on Thursday, and confer with Chirac on Saturday ahead of EU summit.

In other developments, Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg said in an interview with French daily Les Echos that a budget deficit of 3.2 percent would not be a catastrophe for countries wanting to join the euro.
Duisenberg said a delay in EMU could be dangerous for the entire process.

Group of Seven ministeres are likely to discuss recent currency volatility at their next meeting on June 20-22 in Denver, Rubin said. He also said the issue of Japan's trade surplus could come up for discussion at the G7 meeting. He said G7 is likely to discuss recent currency volatility.

September yen held support at $0.008860, which is equivalent to dollar/yen at 114.39 spot. Major support is at $0.008849, or about 114.53. On Wednesday, September yen rose to a six-month high at $0.009174, and fell nearly $0.000400 to $0.008730 on Wednesday's overnight GLOBEX session.

At the end of pit trade, September yen was off $0.000254 at $0.008875, marks fell $0.0048 at $0.5822, Swiss francs were $0.0034 lower at $0.7007, sterling was $0.0062 lower at $1.6280, Canadian dollars were up $0.0018 at $0.7276, Australian dollars were $0.0056 lower at $0.7521 and Mexican pesos were $0.000175 higher at $0.120700.
